previous_statement: Direct nested-comparison threshold bridge. The constant used throughout this proof is chosen as e_s2 := min{1/2, e_nest, e_ncd, e_out, e_sim, e_ca/2}. Hence e_s2 <= e_nest by the defining order property of a finite minimum. The root hypothesis t <= e_s2 then gives t <= e_nest by transitivity. This derivation is universal and dimension-independent and uses no accuracy threshold from lem-extcb-corner-dimension-additivity.
new_statement: Direct nested-comparison threshold bridge, with the final witness distinguished from the preliminary ledger. Let e_s2^0 := min{1/2, e_nest, e_ncd, e_out, e_sim, e_ca/2}. The fixed-source additivity repair in validated node 1.5.2 supplies a further positive universal threshold e_{2,1} and chooses the final root witness e_s2 := min{e_s2^0,e_{2,1}}. Consequently e_s2 <= e_s2^0 by the defining property of a minimum, and e_s2^0 <= e_nest because e_nest is one of the entries defining e_s2^0. Thus the root hypothesis t <= e_s2 gives t <= e_s2 <= e_s2^0 <= e_nest, so the nested-comparison threshold is met. The additivity threshold is used only to shrink the final universal witness; this nested-comparison application itself uses no conclusion of lem-extcb-corner-dimension-additivity.
